plants.sentence: A test statistic is calculated without assuming the null hypothesis is true: it compares the sample statistic with the parameter value in the null and incorporates a standard error.
When a large number of significance tests are run, every one of them will come out significant by chance alone, even if the null hypothesis is true.
With a fixed sample size, decreasing alpha decreases beta and so increases power. To decrease both alpha and beta, decrease the sample size.
Default to a two-sided test, and use a one-sided test only if you truly care about one direction. For a two-sided p-value, compute the p-value for one tail and halve it.
An alpha of 0.05 means a true null hypothesis is rejected 5% of the time. The choice of alpha is somewhat arbitrary, but 0.05 was fixed by Fisher in 1925 and most journals require it.
In one study, quoting a longer delivery time over the phone caused pizzas to arrive 3 minutes early on average, an effect that chance could not explain.
